## Factory review of 3dd0c2b: Request changes

Checks fail: the new default model no longer matches the recorded VCR cassette, so an existing Harbor unit test fails.

| Criterion | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Fit | Pass | does what it claims |
| Checks | Fail | `tests/unit/harbor/test_verify.py` fails (1 of 8) |
| Tests | Fail | existing judge cassette not re-recorded for the new model |
| Blocking findings | 1 | stale `gpt-5-nano` cassette, `evals/harbor/verifiers/harbor_verifiers/llm_judge.py:14` |
| Non-blocking findings | 0 | |
| Risk | Low | side effects: Harbor judge grading moves to a different model |
| Review depth | Focused | eval-harness default plus docs, no public API or schema |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Intent:** Change the Harbor LLM-judge's default `PHOENIX_EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` from `gpt-5-nano` to `gpt-5.6-luna` because `gpt-5-nano` shuts down on 2026-12-11, and update the two READMEs that name the default.
**Fit:** The diff changes the default in `llm_judge.py` and both READMEs, and nothing else. `PHOENIX_EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` still overrides the default. `gpt-5.6-luna` is a model the repo already knows: it appears in the bundled `openai` SDK's `ChatModel` list, in `playground_clients.py` and in `model_cost_manifest.json`.
**Verified:** `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and `mypy` on `llm_judge.py` all pass. `pytest tests/unit/harbor/test_verify.py`, with `evals/harbor/verifiers` importable as tox installs it, gives 1 failed and 7 passed at 3dd0c2b. `test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers` fails with `CannotOverwriteExistingCassetteException` because the request body has `gpt-5.6-luna` and the cassette has `gpt-5-nano`. With `llm_judge.py` set back to `main`, all 8 tests pass. `grep` finds no `gpt-5-nano` left under `evals/harbor`. The only remaining reference is the cassette under `tests/unit/harbor`.
**Not verified:** The live OpenAI API: no key here, so I couldn't check how `gpt-5.6-luna` grades the six cassette cases or whether it accepts the strict `json_schema` response format. The `gpt-5-nano` shutdown date: web search is unavailable in this sandbox. The `harbor-evals` workflow (`make harbor-stage` / `harbor-run`), which needs Daytona and API credentials. The full `unit_tests` tox suite, left to CI. No area reviewer covers `evals/harbor/`, so none was run.
**Findings without a diff line:** none
**Risk:** side effects low (Harbor regression rewards that rely on the judge will now be graded by a different model, so scores may shift against past runs), performance none, backwards compatibility none (env override unchanged). Rated by this review, since no area reviewer covers `evals/harbor/`.

Graded against the [review criteria](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/blob/main/factory/agents/pr-reviewer.md#verdict).

</details>

## Factory review of 2ca3ea8: Request changes

Tests fail: the judge cassette was edited by hand to match the new model, so the grading test replays `gpt-5-nano` answers and says nothing about how `gpt-5.6-luna` grades.

| Criterion | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Fit | Pass | does what it claims |
| Checks | Pass | ruff format/check, mypy (no harbor errors), `tests/unit/harbor` pass |
| Tests | Fail | edited cassette passes whatever the new model does |

| Non-blocking findings | 0 | |
| Risk | Low | side effects: Harbor judge grades with a new model nobody has run |
| Review depth | Focused | eval-harness default, docs and a test fixture; no public API or schema |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Intent:** Change the Harbor LLM judge's default `PHOENIX_EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL` from `gpt-5-nano` to `gpt-5.6-luna`, because the PR says OpenAI shuts `gpt-5-nano` down on 2026-12-11, and update the two READMEs that name the default.
**Fit:** `llm_judge.py:14` and both READMEs now name `gpt-5.6-luna`, and the env override still works. The second commit edits the six request bodies in the judge cassette so the existing test passes again. This fixes the failure the previous factory review found on 3dd0c2b. No `gpt-5-nano` reference is left under `evals/harbor`. `gpt-5.6-luna` is a known model name: it is in the installed `openai` SDK's `ChatModel` list, in `playground_clients.py` and in `model_cost_manifest.json`.
**Verified:** `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` on `evals/harbor/verifiers` and `tests/unit/harbor` pass. `mypy` (the `typecheck-python` config, which covers `evals/`) reports 3 errors, all in files this PR does not touch (`openinference_agent_wrapper.py`, `AnnotationSummary.py`), and none under harbor. `pytest tests/unit/harbor/` with `harbor_verifiers` on the path, as tox installs it, gives 66 passed and 1 skipped (`harbor` is not installed). With `llm_judge.py` set back to `main`, `test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers` fails only on the request-body matcher. So the test now checks the model string, but its six grading assertions still replay `gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07` responses. No area reviewer covers `evals/harbor/` or `tests/unit/harbor/`, so none was run, and this review rated the risk itself.
**Not verified:** The live OpenAI API: there is no key in the sandbox, so I could not check how `gpt-5.6-luna` grades the six cases or whether it accepts the strict `json_schema` response format. The `gpt-5-nano` shutdown date and the replacement model: web search is not available in this sandbox. The `harbor-stage` / `harbor-run` workflow, which needs Daytona and API credentials. The full `unit_tests` tox suite is left to CI.
**Findings without a diff line:** none
**Risk:** side effects low (judge-based Harbor rewards will be graded by a model nobody has run here, so scores may shift against past runs, and if the model rejects strict `json_schema` every judged task fails unless the env var is set), performance none, backwards compatibility none (the env override is unchanged).

Graded against the [review criteria](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/blob/main/factory/agents/pr-reviewer.md#verdict).

</details>

review_comments.body:
**Blocking.** Changing this default breaks `tests/unit/harbor/test_verify.py::test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers`, and the PR doesn't update its cassette.

**Evidence:** The test replays `tests/unit/harbor/cassettes/test_verify/test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers.yaml` with a `_json_bodies_match` matcher that compares the whole request body, `model` included. All six recorded requests have `"model":"gpt-5-nano"` (cassette lines 19, 61, 103, 145, 188, …). The cassette uses `record_mode: "once"`, so at this commit every judge call raises `CannotOverwriteExistingCassetteException` (`_json_bodies_match - assertion failure`, request body `{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna",…}`). I ran `pytest tests/unit/harbor/test_verify.py` with `harbor_verifiers` on the path, as the tox `unit_tests` env installs it: 1 failed, 7 passed. With this line set back to `main`, all 8 pass. The PR's "no other `gpt-5-nano` reference remains" check only covered `evals/harbor`, so it missed the cassette under `tests/unit/harbor`.

**Fix:** With an `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, delete the cassette and re-run the test to record it again against `gpt-5.6-luna`, then commit the new cassette. This also covers the "Not run against the live API" gap in the PR body. It shows the new model accepts the judge's strict `json_schema` `response_format` and still gives the six expected match/mismatch grades.

**Blocking.** The cassette was edited by hand, so `test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers` now passes on a fake pairing: the six request bodies say `"model":"gpt-5.6-luna"`, but every replayed response is still the `gpt-5-nano` recording.

**Evidence:** Lines 19, 61, 103, 145, 188 and 229 send `gpt-5.6-luna`. The responses right after them (lines 27, 69, 111, 153, 196, 237) still contain `"model": "gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07"`. The commit message and the author's comment both say the responses were not re-recorded. Because of this, the test's six match/mismatch assertions would still pass if `gpt-5.6-luna` graded these replies differently or rejected the judge's strict `json_schema` `response_format`. The only part tied to this PR is the model string. I set `llm_judge.py` back to `main` and the test failed only on the body matcher. This goes against REVIEW.md § Always Check ("Tests MUST fail when the behavior they cover is removed — tests that only exercise mocks … MUST NOT be added").

**Fix:** With an `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, delete this cassette and run `pytest tests/unit/harbor/test_verify.py::test_reference_check_grades_semantic_answers` to record it again against `gpt-5.6-luna` (`record_mode: "once"` records when the file is missing). Then commit the new recording. If the new model grades any case differently, update the expected scores or the template. A maintainer with a key may need to do this, as the author offered.
